sources.citation: Rodríguez Fuentes, Antonio, Lineth Alaín & Francisco García García. 2020. EnSenias: herramienta tecnológica para aprender, enseñar, mejorar y usar la lengua de signos panameña. Íkala 25(3). 16 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; app validation study, no linguistic description (a full-text search for stress/accent fonolog/prosod/acento/entonación returns no hits).

sources.citation: Alaín Botacio, Lineth. 2019. Desarrollo y validación de una aplicación Web y CD educativa inclusiva para el aprendizaje de la Lengua de Señas Panameña. Tesis doctoral, Universidad de Granada (dir. A. Rodríguez Fuentes, F. García García). 406 pp. ISBN 9788413062440.
sources.note: Nothing on prosody or stress. Educational-technology thesis (EnSenias app, 1,253 signs). Ch.1 pp.54-55 gives a generic sign-language 'querología' paragraph (seven formational parameters: handshape, place, planes, movement, orientation, contact, non-manual) attributed to García 2015, not specific to LSP. p.58: 'A la fecha de 2019 no existe un diccionario de la LSP' and no studies of LSP origins by Panamanian Deaf/interpreters exist. Cites no LSP grammar.

sources.citation: Parks, Elizabeth, Holly Williams & Jason Parks. 2014. Perfil Sociolingüístico de los Sordos de Panamá. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2014-008. Dallas: SIL International. 18 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Rapid-appraisal sociolinguistic survey (Oct 2009). p.10 inventories all LSP print materials: ANSPA early-1980s primer 'Programa de Comunicación Total: Lenguaje de Señas y Deletreo' (word list, no illustrations); ANSPA 1990 'Lengua de Señas Panameñas' (207 pp. line drawings, many reportedly copied from a LESCO dictionary); and Garay 2004, described as 'un CD instructivo diseñado para enseñar la diferencia entre LSP y ASL' — i.e. Glottolog's only 'grammar sketch' is a teaching CD, not a description.

sources.citation: Holbrook, David J. 2007 (2007-12-13). Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Panamanian Sign Language [lsp], change request 2008-024. 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Section 5c 'Knowledge from published sources' lists only Garay 2004 ('An instructional CD designed to teach Spanish Sign Language vs. American Sign Language for the Panama International Deaf Society, published by Asociación Nacional de Sordos de Panamá') and the ANSPA 1990 dictionary 'Lengua de señas panameñas'. No grammar or phonology is known to the requester.

sources.citation: Parks, Elizabeth S. 2016. Identifying overlapping language communities: the case of Chiriquí and Panamanian signed languages. Multilingua 35(3): 305-330.
